answer: In an agent marketplace arranging a voyage to an island that exports onyx, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. The bond cannot back two identities at once, so an attacker running 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million for a month. Creating new keys does not evade the requirement: every accepted bid is checked against its identity’s funded, still-locked bond on a public ledger.
